note: lower_bound gives the first not-less element; upper_bound the first greater. The gap is the run.
find_if returns end() on failure, so always compare against end() before dereferencing.
accumulate's init argument sets the result type: pass 0.0, not 0, when summing doubles.
Both set algorithms require sorted input; on unsorted ranges they silently give nonsense.
all_of on an empty range is true and any_of is false; the vacuous cases catch people out.
sort is not stable and can reorder equal elements; stable_sort costs more and never does.
unique only collapses adjacent duplicates, so sort first unless adjacency is what you meant.
from_chars never allocates, never throws and never looks at the locale, unlike stoi.
Use steady_clock for elapsed time; system_clock can jump backwards when the wall clock is adjusted.
Durations convert implicitly only when no precision is lost; narrowing needs duration_cast.
priority_queue is a max-heap by default; pass std::greater to invert it.
map keeps keys ordered in O(log n); unordered_map is O(1) average with no order at all.
vector reallocates and invalidates everything; deque only invalidates iterators, not references.
multiset keeps duplicates; equal_range hands you the whole run of equal keys at once.
A comparator must be a strict weak ordering: comp(a, a) has to be false or the sort corrupts memory.
Combine field hashes with a shift and xor; adding them collides on any permutation.
remove only shuffles survivors forward and returns the new logical end; erase does the shrinking.
Random access gives O(1) distance; a forward iterator has to walk, so the tag picks the algorithm.
back_inserter turns an output iterator into push_back, so the destination grows as needed.
value() throws on empty; value_or never does. Pick deliberately, do not mix them by accident.
The projection argument removes the need for a comparator lambda in most sorts.
views::join flattens one level of nesting lazily, without building the intermediate container.
Views are lazy and composable: nothing is computed until you iterate the final range.
span is a pointer plus a length, so one function signature accepts array, vector and C buffer.
A string_view does not own anything, so never return one that points at a local string.
Streaming into a variable sets failbit on bad input, so test the stream before trusting the value.
tie builds a tuple of references, which is why it can both destructure and compare in one line.
An overload set built from lambdas is how you write a type switch that the compiler checks.
